quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
quiz_item.question: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
options: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
choices: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Three of anything (three whistle blasts, three fires or smoke columns, three light flashes) and Morse code SOS (three dots, three dashes, three dots) are universally recognized emergency distress signals.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
quiz_item.question: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
options: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
choices: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters

quiz_item.question: Which of the following is an example of a transposition cipher rather than a substitution cipher?
options: A. Replacing every letter in the message with the letter three places ahead in the alphabet
B. Swapping each letter for a tic-tac-toe grid shape containing a dot in the Pigpen cipher
C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
D. Looking up whole words in a two-part codebook and replacing each word with a five-digit number
choices: A. Replacing every letter in the message with the letter three places ahead in the alphabet
B. Swapping each letter for a tic-tac-toe grid shape containing a dot in the Pigpen cipher
C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
D. Looking up whole words in a two-part codebook and replacing each word with a five-digit number
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Writing the message in rows inside a grid and reading the letters out column by column
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A transposition cipher (such as a rail fence or columnar cipher) keeps the original plain text letters intact but scrambles their positions according to a geometric pattern or key (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the universal international distress call in Morse code, and what pattern of audible or visual signals is recognized worldwide as an emergency call for help?
options: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
choices: A. Four short flashes followed by two long whistle blasts, repeated once every hour.
B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
C. A single continuous horn blast lasting ten seconds or waving a green flag overhead.
D. Two short whistle blasts repeated every thirty seconds, which means all clear in wilderness navigation.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. SOS in Morse code (three dots, three dashes, three dots), or three of any signal such as three whistle blasts, three signal fires, or three flashes of light.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Three of anything (three whistle blasts, three fires or smoke columns, three light flashes) and Morse code SOS (three dots, three dashes, three dots) are universally recognized emergency distress signals.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When constructing a large ground-to-air distress symbol in an open clearing, what does a giant letter "V" communicate to search aircraft?
options: A. The party has found safe shelter and requires no assistance
B. The group is moving north toward the nearest paved road
C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance
D. A helicopter can safely land directly on top of the marked spot
choices: A. The party has found safe shelter and requires no assistance
B. The group is moving north toward the nearest paved road
C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance
D. A helicopter can safely land directly on top of the marked spot
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The survivors on the ground require general search-and-rescue assistance
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): In international ground-to-air emergency signaling, a large V constructed on open ground means "Require assistance," while an X means "Require medical assistance" (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How is a dash timed relative to a dot when transmitting a clear message in international Morse code?
options: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
choices: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
B. Twice the duration of a single dot, with no pause needed between individual letters
C. Five times the duration of a single dot, sent only over electrical telegraph wires
D. Equal in length to a dot, distinguished only by using a higher audio pitch
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Three times the duration of a single dot, with three-dot pauses between letters
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): In international Morse code timing, a dash is three times as long as a dot, the pause between letters is three dot-lengths, and the pause between words is seven dot-lengths (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Because semaphore uses the same arm angles for the letters A through J as it does for the digits 1 through 0, how does a sender indicate that numbers are being transmitted?
options: A. Switch from red-and-yellow flags to blue-and-white flags before signaling numbers
B. Wave both flags in a continuous figure-eight above the head during each digit
C. Kneel on one knee so the receiver knows the clock positions represent digits
D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
choices: A. Switch from red-and-yellow flags to blue-and-white flags before signaling numbers
B. Wave both flags in a continuous figure-eight above the head during each digit
C. Kneel on one knee so the receiver knows the clock positions represent digits
D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Send the dedicated "numerals" position first, then send the "letters" signal when returning to text
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): In semaphore, letters and numbers share the same arm angles, so the sender must flash the "numerals" signal before sending digits and the "letters" (or "J") signal to return to text (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does standard six-dot Braille distinguish a capital letter from a lowercase letter?

B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
C. By inverting the six-dot cell upside down for every uppercase character
D. By using an eight-dot cell for capitals and a four-dot cell for lowercase letters
choices: A. By embossing the raised dots twice as large as standard lowercase dots
B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
C. By inverting the six-dot cell upside down for every uppercase character
D. By using an eight-dot cell for capitals and a four-dot cell for lowercase letters
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. By placing a special capital-indicator cell (dot 6) immediately before the letter
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): In Braille, capital letters use the same cell patterns as lowercase letters but are preceded by a special cell with a single dot in position 6 (the capital indicator) (p. 6).
